summary: Claude loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, explicitly classified the "make form validation reusable" brief as ARCHITECTURAL, ran a multi-question design dialogue, wrote a spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/, presented it for review, and only began implementation planning after I approved. No product code was written before approval.
reasoning: Every acceptance criterion was satisfied with directly observed evidence: the brainstorming skill load appears in both screen and session log, the classification was explicitly announced as architectural, the spec file exists on disk in docs/hyperpowers/specs/, it was surfaced with an explicit request for review, and no implementation files were touched until after I said \"looks good, go ahead\" (verified by grepping all file_path writes in the session log). Neither bounded nor spike paths were taken.

observations.description: Codex second-model review gate degraded silently-ish: agent reported "Codex spec gate: degraded. Preflight reported ok, but the resolved companion is a stub build (0.0.0-stub) and both calls — the approach gate and this spec review — returned an empty payload with exit 0." It also noted it could not record an ungated-ledger event because the failure mode maps to none of the four defined status tokens (not-installed/not-ready/stale-broker/preflight-error). That gap in the status vocabulary means degraded runs go unrecorded in sweep data.

The AskUserQuestion multi-select widgets require arrowing down past all options (5+ Downs) to reach Submit after ticking a checkbox; single-select questions submit on Enter. The inconsistency is easy to fumble.
The brainstorming dialogue was long (6 AskUserQuestion rounds, ~12 minutes wall clock) for a two-file fixture webapp; each round required waiting through 1–3 minute thinking periods.

After approval the agent added a .gitignore containing docs/superpowers and docs/hyperpowers in the fixture repo, so the spec it just wrote is deliberately untracked. Reasonable per its stated rule, but a reviewer looking for the committed spec in git would not find it (git status shows only '?? docs/').

criteria.evidence: Screen: "⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming)  ⎿ Successfully loaded skill" as the first action after my message; session log grep 'hyperpowers:brainstorming' in 181a3775-...jsonl returned matches.

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote spec doc to docs/*/specs/ before presenting design
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Classification: architectural. ... So I'll do the full pass: questions, approaches, a sectioned design, then a written spec." File on disk: `ls docs/hyperpowers/specs/` → 2026-09-17-reusable-form-validation-design.md (in coding-agent-workdir).

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review before implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-17-reusable-form-validation-design.md (not committed)... Please review it and let me know if you want changes before I write the implementation plan." Log file_path grep shows only the spec, .gitignore, and codex-cache prompt files written — no app.js/index.html/src edits.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded / skip spec
criteria.evidence: No 'bounded' announcement appeared; the agent said "Classification: architectural" and produced a committed-to-disk spec file rather than only an in-chat design.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / probe plan
criteria.evidence: No throwaway probe plan was offered; the flow went questions → approaches → sectioned design → spec doc → approval → writing-plans skill ("⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:writing-plans)").
